Information since June points to a robust labor market and strong real activity with inflation near the symmetric 2% objective and expectations little changed. In standard policy-rule frameworks with feedback to economic conditions, such an environment supports gradual rate increases to stabilize inflation and output while maintaining maximum employment. At the same time, the literature emphasizes that higher interest rates have a contractionary impact on real activity—especially investment and hiring—via tighter credit conditions and financing constraints, and with nominal wage/price rigidities these effects are real in the short run. Given the Committee’s continued accommodative stance, balanced risk assessment, and reliance on a wide information set (labor, inflation pressures/expectations, and financial/international developments), the overall tone is positive but measured rather than exuberant.
